crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: GDP Nowcasting
children.blurb: GDP nowcasting is the practice of estimating current-quarter GDP growth before official statistics are published, using higher-frequency data that arrive during the quarter.

children.name: Reading Central Bank Communication
children.blurb: This page covers the use of natural language processing and machine learning to read central bank communication, including policy statements, meeting minutes, speeches, and press conference transcripts.

children.name: Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis
children.blurb: Synthetic populations are artificial datasets of individuals, households, or firms designed to mirror the statistical properties of a real population while containing no actual personal records.

children.name: Climate and the Economy
children.blurb: Climate and the economy sits at the intersection of macroeconomic forecasting, environmental accounting, and policy evaluation.

children.name: Agent-Based and Game Theory Models
children.blurb: Agent-based and game theory models in macroeconomic econometrics simulate economies as populations of heterogeneous agents who interact according to strategic rules, rather than as a single representative household or firm.

sections.body: Macroeconomic econometrics uses AI to measure and forecast broad economic conditions from data that is messy, high frequency, or unstructured. In practice, machine learning models now read satellite images of parking lots and night lights to estimate activity, parse millions of job postings for labour demand, and turn central bank speeches into sentiment scores. These tools feed into nowcasts of GDP growth, inflation, and employment that update daily or weekly instead of quarterly. They also simulate large populations of households and firms to test how a tax change or subsidy might ripple through spending. The work is descriptive and predictive, not prescriptive.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has made real progress on short horizon forecasting and text classification. GDP nowcasting models often match or beat simple statistical benchmarks for the current quarter, and central bank language models can reliably label hawkish and dovish statements. What remains unsolved is longer horizon forecasting, causal inference from observational data, and reliable behaviour under rare events like financial crises or pandemics. Synthetic populations can reproduce aggregate distributions but struggle to capture how real people change their behaviour when policy changes. Honest limits include data revisions, nonstationarity, and the fact that many economic relationships shift for reasons no model trained on the past can foresee.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with GDP Nowcasting to see how high frequency indicators are combined into a single current quarter estimate. Reading Central Bank Communication then shows how the same text modelling ideas are applied to policy language and market expectations. Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis moves from measurement to simulation, explaining how agent level data is used to test policy counterfactuals. Climate and the Economy extends these methods to physical risk, energy transition, and damage functions where data is sparse and horizons are long. Agent-Based and Game Theory Models closes the section by relaxing the representative agent assumption and modelling strategic interaction, which connects back to the limits of the earlier forecasting pages.
